voice: Kāṇha, the kāpālika yogi, sings straight at Ḍombī, the outcaste woman whose hut is outside the town: he courts her, needles her with a question, flaunts his bones for her, and ends on a flat threat to kill her. Blunt spoken English in short clauses, the call 'Hey' kept sharp, nothing softened in the desire or the menace.

lines.en: touching, touching, goes that [brahmin]{brahmin} with the shaven crown.
Hey, I'll keep company with you, [Ḍombī]{dombi};
in whose [boat]{boat} do you come and go, [Ḍombī]{dombi}?
for your sake I've given up the performer's basket.
For your sake I've put on a [garland of bones]{bone-garland}.
I'll kill [Ḍombī]{dombi}, I'll take her life.

couplets.kept: The full rhyme kuṛiā/nāṛiā becomes town/crown, with 'town' moved to the end of 1a. The doubled chaichoi stays doubled as 'touching, touching', in the accurate's sense, and 'that brahmin' keeps its demonstrative.
couplets.letGo: 'Shaven-headed' is sung as 'with the shaven crown' for the rhyme, which may suggest a tonsure. The accurate's 'goes by' is sung as the source's bare 'goes'. 1b runs longer than 1a, reversing the source's proportions.

couplets.kept: The refrain and Kāṇha's self-naming stay whole, and 'Hey' keeps the call's bite. Ending the lines on 'Ḍombī' and 'yogi' answers the near rhyme sāṅga/lāga with a light echo and sets the two figures side by side.
couplets.letGo: 'Hey' is parted from 'Ḍombī', which the source keeps together (ālo ḍombi). The echo is weaker than the source's near rhyme, and 'without disgust' now sits by the verb instead of directly on Kāṇha.

couplets.kept: The single lotus keeps its sixty-four petals, and 'poor' stays as open as in the accurate English. Both lines end on a falling two-syllable word, as the source ends on -khuṛī and -puṛī.
couplets.letGo: The full rhyme pākhuṛī/bāpuṛī is let go: no English rhyme for 'petals' or 'dances' comes without adding a word or bending the order.

couplets.kept: The call 'Hey Ḍombī' opens the line as in the source, and the question keeps its edge. 'Honestly' and the name moved to the end make a slant rhyme for the full rhyme sadabhābe/nābem̐.
couplets.letGo: 'In good faith' becomes the plainer 'honestly' and loses a little formality. The source line ends on 'boat'; the sung line ends on the name.

couplets.kept: Sings the accurate's open 'no more baskets'. 'For your sake' uses the same words as 6b, as tohora antare recurs there. The line-end echo baskets/basket stands in for the near rhyme caṅgatā/eṭṭā.
couplets.letGo: The echo repeats one English word where the source has two different, uncertain words (caṅgatā and (p)eṭṭā), so it can sound like a repetition the source does not make.

couplets.kept: The blunt pairing of you and I, two outcastes, is clipped into two short clauses, with 'girl' for lo. 'For your sake' repeats 5b's words, and 'I've given up' there is answered by 'I've put on' here.
couplets.letGo: The full rhyme kapālī/mālī is let go: 'kāpālika' and 'garland of bones' offer no honest English rhyme.

couplets.kept: The paired first-person verbs mārami … lemi become 'I'll kill … I'll take', and a chime runs from 'Breaking the lake' to 'take her life'. The threat stays flat and unsoftened.
couplets.letGo: The full end rhyme molāṇa/parāṇa is let go: 'root' and 'life' do not rhyme, and no honest reordering makes them.

questions: Refrain (2a): I moved 'Ḍombī' to the end of the line ('Hey, I'll keep company with you, Ḍombī') for a light echo with 'yogi' at the end of 2b. If you prefer the source's call and name together, the unrhymed alternative is 'Hey Ḍombī, I'll keep company with you', and the refrain cue would become 'Hey Ḍombī, I'll keep company'.

1b: is 'with the shaven crown' acceptable for nāṛiā 'shaven-headed', given that 'crown' can suggest a tonsure rather than a fully shaven head? The unrhymed fallback is 'touching, touching, goes that shaven-headed brahmin'.
4a: I sang sadabhābe as 'honestly' (the accurate has 'in good faith'). It is plainer and gives a slant rhyme with 'Ḍombī' at the end of 4b. Keep it, or return to 'in good faith' and let the rhyme go?

5a/5b: following the accurate English, two different source words (caṅgatā and (p)eṭṭā) both come out as 'basket', which in a sung version sounds like a deliberate repetition. Should the performer's (p)eṭṭā be sung as 'box' (within the gloss 'basket/box') to keep them apart, at the cost of the echo?

Refrain cue placement: the source prints ধ্রু after couplet 1 as well, before the refrain has been sung (the accurate draft also raises this). I have assumed the cue is printed only after couplets 3 to 7. Please confirm.
